extracted.intended_audience: general readers, librarians, and others interested in children's literature and book awards
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the standards and procedural facts for the Caldecott Medal: an annual American award given to the artist of the most distinguished American picture book for children, presented by the American Library Association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary award standard — 'most distinguished American picture book for children'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Caldecott Medal is an annual prize awarded “to the artist of the most distinguished American picture book for children.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This phrase is the core evaluative standard used to choose the winner; the Britannica entry does not further define 'most distinguished' on this page, but it implies judgment of overall excellence in a picture book's artistic/illustrative merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient requirement — awarded to the artist (illustrator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded 'to the artist' of the picture book; in winners' listings the author is shown in parentheses if different from the illustrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The medal recognizes the book's artist/illustrator rather than (primarily) the author; the winners table and note '*Author in parentheses if different from illustrator.' illustrate this procedural/crediting convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility scope — American picture book for children
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is limited to 'American' picture books intended for children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Britannica states the nationality/scope as 'American' but does not further specify on this page how 'American' is defined (e.g., by author/illustrator nationality, publisher, or place of publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation/procedural detail — presented at ALA annual conference
rubrics_metrics.description: The Caldecott Medal is presented at the annual conference of the American Library Association, together with the Newbery Medal for children's literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural fact about how and where the award is given (annual ALA conference); the entry does not provide selection-process details beyond the award standard.
